documents.label: A
documents.citation: Herbert Hoover, Press Statement on the Economy, October 25, 1929 (National Archives, public domain)
documents.excerpt: The fundamental business of the country — that is, production and distribution of commodities — is on a sound and prosperous basis...I have no fear of the fundamental strength of our business and economic structure.

documents.label: B
documents.citation: Franklin D. Roosevelt, First Inaugural Address, March 4, 1933 (National Archives, public domain)
documents.excerpt: The money changers have fled from their high seats in the temple of our civilization. We may now restore that temple to the ancient truths. The measure of the restoration lies in the extent to which we apply social values more noble than mere monetary profit...Happiness lies not in the mere possession of money; it lies in the joy of achievement, in the thrill of creative effort. The joy and moral stimulation of work no longer must be forgotten in the mad chase of evanescent profits.

documents.label: C
documents.citation: Senate Finance Committee testimony of Marriner Eccles (Federal Reserve Chairman nominee), February 5, 1935 (Congressional Record, public domain)
documents.excerpt: Mass production has to be accompanied by mass consumption...As long as we continue to render the masses of people increasingly impotent economically, we shall not be able to bring about recovery. We must find ways of increasing their purchasing power.
